claims.quote: And sooner or later, no doubt, the numerous advantages of such an arrangement will lead to the organization of large carrier companies, using such motor trucks to carry goods in bulk or parcels on the high roads.
claims.description: Large trucking companies are predicted to form and carry freight on the roads.

claims.quote: It will be capable of a day’s journey of three hundred miles or more, long before the developments to be presently foreshadowed arrive.
claims.description: Privately owned motor cars are predicted to travel 300 miles or more in a single day.

claims.quote: This segregation of motor traffic is probably a matter that may begin even in the present decade.
claims.description: Motor vehicles are predicted to be separated onto their own roads, starting within the decade.

claims.quote: they will attempt to secure, and, it may be, after tough legislative struggles, will secure the power to form private roads of a new sort, upon which their vehicles will be free to travel up to the limit of their very highest possible speed.
claims.description: Motor-bus companies are predicted to win legal rights to build private high-speed roads for their vehicles.

claims.quote: They will have to be very wide—they will be just as wide as the courage of their promoters goes—and if the first made are too narrow there will be no question of gauge to limit the later ones.
claims.description: Dedicated motor roads are predicted to be built much wider than existing roads, with no fixed width standard.

claims.quote: For example, they will be very different from macadamized roads; they will be used only by soft-tired conveyances
claims.description: The new motor roads are predicted to use soft-tired vehicles only, with a surface unlike macadam.

claims.quote: it is perhaps more probable they will be made of very good asphalt sloped to drain, and still more probable that they will be of some quite new substance altogether
claims.description: The surface of the new motor roads is guessed to be asphalt or a new material.

claims.quote: where their ways branch the streams of traffic will not cross at a level but by bridges.
claims.description: Motor roads are predicted to cross each other on bridges, not at grade.

claims.quote: it may be that some at least of the railway companies will hasten to replace their flanged rolling stock by carriages with rubber tyres, remove their rails, broaden their cuttings and embankments, raise their bridges, and take to the new ways of traffic.
claims.description: Some railway companies may convert to rubber-tired carriages on road-like tracks to compete with motor roads.

claims.quote: There is, however, one conceivable means of transit that is not simply frequent but continuous, that may be joined or left at any point without a stoppage
claims.description: A continuous moving platform on which passengers step on and off without stopping is imagined for city transit.

claims.quote: we should have the upper platform running round the circle at a pace of twenty-eight miles an hour.
claims.description: Stacked moving platforms in a city loop are calculated to carry the top platform at about 28 miles per hour.

claims.quote: Almost insensibly, certain highly profitable longer routes will be joined up—the London to Brighton, for example, in England.
claims.description: Long-distance motor routes such as London to Brighton are predicted to be linked into a network.

claims.quote: read one day with surprise in the violently illustrated popular magazines of 1910, that there are now so many thousand miles of these roads already established in America and Germany and elsewhere.
claims.description: Thousands of miles of dedicated motor roads are predicted to exist in America and Germany by 1910.

claims.quote: These things may be the first beginning of a process of restriction that may go far.
claims.description: Limits on heavy street traffic are predicted to grow into wider restrictions on city vehicles.

claims.quote: And step by step with these developments will come a very considerable acceleration of the ferry traffic of the narrow seas through such improvements as the introduction of turbine engines.
claims.description: Channel ferries are predicted to get much faster with the introduction of turbine engines.
